script_corrections: I1/I2: a first development run (--runs 2) failed every row on an extra check of my own, 'candidate.resolved equals the committed Dn run's git_ref'; the prereg does not ask for it and it cannot hold: a clone's commit message carries the clone's name (`probe <name>`), so the sha differs from the committed run's although the tree is the same. The check is now 'resolved is the commit that was fetched as dN'. No pass rule of the prereg changed.
procedure: Helpers: JCtx and SX (exclude_probes.py: Ctx subclasses of probes.py and streak_probes.py) are reused; the manifests of the multi-consumer workspaces (I4) are written here. A candidate ref dN is the committed edit list applied to a clone of the clean clone (`ctx.clone`, the runners' fixed author and dates, so the sha is the committed Dn's) and fetched into the provider clone as refs/heads/dN, before the measured window.

Each run of a deterministic probe makes the --json call and the text call; the canonical record holds both (the JSON without elapsed_s). Scratch paths are scrubbed to $WORK only when written out; equality across the 10 runs is on the raw canonical records.

'= committed Dn' compares the row's `findings` and `gaps` with `links[0]` of `runs[0]` of the committed data file (job-scheduler D/C: runs[0].doc; Streak D: runs[0].check.doc; Streak C: runs[0].doc; exclude X2: runs[0].check_after_pin.doc, X3: runs[0].r6_check.doc).

I6: a `sitecustomize` in a directory first on PYTHONPATH logs every Popen argv and socket connect (append-only file outside TMPDIR). Allowed argv: `git` with a subcommand in {rev-parse, ls-tree, cat-file, status} (global options skipped) or the export child (`-m lattice.contracts export`); export children counted from the Popen events of the call. The snapshot covers the probe's workspace directory (manifest variants, consumers), its provider clone(s), any candidate directory the call names and the lattice-impact worktree (the --out directory excluded); 'newer' is a file whose mtime is later than the call's start (the find -newer rule). I7's MCP and API calls are traced from the request (the server's start-up is not part of the call).

I4 workspaces: A = scheduler (clean clone, spec.tickets:t5), ci-bot, ci-bot-2 (the `POST /auth/login` and `GET /applications` tables of ci-bot); B = scheduler, streak, multi (ci-bot's 7 and streak-widget's 7 tables) with static links to both. ci-bot-2 and multi are pinned with `contracts pin` on the clean clones.

I8: the three runners run as subprocesses with --runs and read their last line; pytest and dogfood/studio/check.sh run in this process' environment (UV_NO_SYNC set); the byte comparison runs the same argv under PYTHONPATH=<this tree> and PYTHONPATH=<the main checkout at 67189af> on the I1 workspace; `pin` writes into two copies of the consumer.
